raw_case_text: A 21-year-old female from hilly area of Kashmir, presented with pus discharge of from two openings on the right breast for last 6 years. These aberrant openings on breast had often spontaneous pus discharge followed by cessation of discharge on its own. There were neither any constitutional symptoms nor any discharge or any abnormality of the nipple. She had already taken antitubercular therapy (ATT) thrice but was defaulter all times and reluctant for further antitubercular therapy (ATT) intake. Systemic examination was normal. Local examination showed no abnormality in left breast. A 1.5 centimeter opening was seen in inferior and outer quadrant breast, through which whitish pus was discharging along with a scar superior to discharging sinus which used to discharge pus 2 weeks before. (Figure 1). No swelling was palpable. Two firm tracts, inferior one with length of 4 cm, superior with 2.5 cm, were run posterior-superiorly ending on fifth rib. No axillary lymphadenopathy was evident. Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) was raised. Montoux test was positive (16x14 mm). X-ray chest showed an osteolytic lesion in anterior part of fifth rib. Computed tomography scan of chest could not reveal any foci of tuberculosis in lungs; only two sinus tracts in breast tissue and the necrosed rib were seen. Purulent aspirate was sterile for tubercle bacilli. Breast ultrasound showed ill-defined sinus tract and opening. Given the reluctance to antitubercular therapy (ATT) intake and recurrent disease coupled with apprehension of further followup, surgical intervention was done through fifth intercostal space. Excision of fibrous tract and resection of involved rib were carried out. (Figures 2 and 3) About 12 cm of rib containing pus and necrosed tissue were resected. Histopathology of specimen was chronic inflammatory cell infiltrate, with areas of caseous necrosis, giant cells (Figure 4). After proper counseling and understanding the nature of disease by patient and her parents the affected woman was motivated for antitubercular therapy (ATT) intake and with daily dose of 300 mg isoniazid, 600 mg rifampicin, 1500 mg pyrazinamide, ethambutol, and 10 mg pyridoxine for 9 months. She had regularly attended our followup clinics during last two years, with no recurrence of disease being recorded.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 21-year-old female presenting with chronic pus discharge from two right breast sinuses for six years.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient presented with a 6-year history of persistent whitish pus discharge from two abnormal sinuses on her right breast. The sinuses discharged spontaneously with intermittent temporary cessation followed by recurrence. She noted no nipple discharge or retraction and no constitutional symptoms. She had previously been prescribed antitubercular therapy on three separate occasions, but had defaulted treatment each time due to reluctance to take medications.
subjective.past_medical_history: Resides in a hilly area of Kashmir. History of breast tuberculosis with three prior defaulted courses of antituberculosis therapy (ATT). Denies other chronic medical conditions.
subjective.review_of_systems: Pus discharge from right breast sinuses. Denies fever, chills, night sweats, weight loss, anorexia, breast pain, or nipple discharge.

objective.physical_examination: Systemic physical examination was normal. Left breast examination was normal. Right breast examination revealed a 1.5 cm cutaneous sinus in the inferior-outer quadrant discharging whitish pus, with a healed scar superior to it from a previous sinus tract. No palpable breast masses. Two firm subcutaneous tracts were palpated coursing posterosuperiorly toward the chest wall (inferior tract 4 cm, superior tract 2.5 cm) terminating on the fifth rib. No axillary lymphadenopathy was palpable.
objective.routine_investigations: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) was elevated. Mantoux tuberculin test was positive (16 x 14 mm induration). Chest radiograph showed an osteolytic lesion in the anterior aspect of the right fifth rib. Breast ultrasound showed ill-defined sinus tracts and cutaneous openings.
objective.advanced_workup: Chest CT scan showed no active pulmonary parenchymal tuberculous lesions, confirming two sinus tracts traversing the breast tissue and osteolytic necrosis of the fifth rib. Purulent sinus aspirate was sterile for pyogenic bacteria and tubercle bacilli on routine culture. Excisional surgery through the fifth intercostal space was performed, with complete resection of the fibrous sinus tracts and 12 cm of the involved necrotic fifth rib containing pus.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation:
Definitive diagnosis: Secondary breast tuberculosis with tuberculous osteomyelitis of the fifth rib and chest wall cold abscess forming chronic discharging fistulae, in a multi-defaulting patient.
Diagnostic confirmation: Histopathological examination of the resected rib and sinus tracts demonstrated chronic inflammatory infiltrate with extensive caseous necrosis and Langhans giant cells, alongside radiographic osteolytic rib destruction and positive Mantoux test.
Management and outcome: Radical excision of sinus tracts and en bloc resection of 12 cm of necrotic rib. Following extensive adherence counseling, the patient was successfully initiated on a 9-month daily antituberculosis regimen: isoniazid 300 mg, rifampicin 600 mg, pyrazinamide 1500 mg, ethambutol, and pyridoxine 10 mg. She regularly attended follow-up clinic for 2 years with complete wound healing and no recurrence.
